newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts finish up sharply.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts finish up sharply.

text.p: NYMEX front-month Henry Hub gas futures, boosted early by panicked shorts and cold weather, rallied to new highs again Wednesday in near-record trade, then eased on ACCESS on profit taking after recent gains.

December rallied 32.1 cents to close at $3.627 per million British thermal units after hitting a new high of $3.65. January, which also set a new benchmark of $3.34, settled 9.4 cents higher at $3.264. Others ended mixed.
"This is a classic short squeeze. It's a technical runaway, but there's also a lot of fundamental support too," said Chris Bray at United Fuels in Massachusetts.

Bray said concerns about low storage and forecasts for much colder weather through the month helped fuel the recent bullish tide. December futures, which expire Thursday, have surged 37 percent in the last five sessions.

December, which closed today at the highest level ever for a spot month, slipped early on ACCESS to the $3.55 level on profit taking after the weekly AGA storage report, but rebounded by 1730 EST to the $3.60-61 level.

"Even though the (AGA) draw was at the high end of expectations, people used it as an opportunity to exit some length," said one Midwest trader, noting the market was due at some point for a profit taking pullback.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 86 bcf to 82 percent of capacity. Overall inventories were still 181 bcf, or six percent, below year-ago, but storage in the critical Consuming Region East was at 92 percent full and still slightly above last year.
Chartists still pegged December resistance at the all-time spot continuation intraday high of $3.72 from last December. Support was seen at $3.10 and then at $2.88.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices jumped almost 40 cents Wednesday to the high-$3.30s. Midwest pipes gained a similar amount to the low-to-mid $3.20s. New York city gate swing gas also was up almost 40 cents to near the $4 level, with December in New York quoted at $1.30-35 over the NYMEX screen.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 4.5 cents to $2.444. NYMEX said 94,262 Hub contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally 77,119 and near the record of 97,916 seen on December 21, 1995.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas closed 15 cents higher at $1.90. Deferred contracts settled up by one to 18.5 cents. NYMEX said 33 Alberta contracts traded versus four on Tuesday.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded but December settled 50 cents higher at $3.45.

On the KCBT, December finished 57.2 cents higher at $3.622, while forward months ended up by one to 10 cents. The East/West spread collapsed 25.1 cents Wednesday to one-half cent (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 1,001 contracts traded, up from Friday's total of 851.
KCBT December natgas expires Friday, November 22.
